```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Choi_2018_kaurenoic_acid"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Choi_2018_kaurenoic_acid"))$description`
* Article (open access): <https://doi.org/10.3390/pharmaceutics10040253>

Kaurenoic acid (KAU) is a diterpene from the root of *Aralia continentalis*
Kitagawa (Araliae continentalis Radix), an herbal extract powder approved in
Korea for pain and convulsion. Choi et al. developed a UPLC-MS/MS assay with
an LLOQ of 0.2 ng/mL and used it to describe the first human PK profile of
KAU after the usual clinical dose of the extract. The concentration-time data
were fitted with the naive-pooled engine of Phoenix NLME 8.0; a
two-compartment model with first-order absorption and no lag time was
selected over one-compartment and lag-time alternatives (Results 3.4).

# Population

Ten healthy Korean men aged 21-33 years (mean 25.8), weighing 60.4-86.7 kg
(mean 73.3), with creatinine clearance 98.0-139.1 mL/min (mean 115.0) took a
single oral dose of 1.0054 g extract powder, which contained 1.147 mg KAU
(Results 3.1), with 240 mL water after a fast of at least 10 h. Plasma was
sampled before the dose and at 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10 and
12 h (Methods 2.5). Demographics are in Choi 2018 Table 3.

The same information is available programmatically:

```{r population}
str(rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Choi_2018_kaurenoic_acid"))$population)
```

# Source trace

| Equation / parameter | Value | Source location |
|----------------------|-------|-----------------|
| `lka` (ka)    | 1.72 1/h  | Table 4, Ka (CV 28.79%) |
| `lcl` (CL/F)  | 23.89 L/h | Table 4, CL/F (CV 9.30%) |
| `lvc` (V/F)   | 24.44 L   | Table 4, V/F (CV 29.16%) |
| `lq` (CLD/F)  | 15.55 L/h | Table 4, CLD/F (CV 13.77%) |
| `lvp` (V2/F)  | 64.05 L   | Table 4, V2/F (CV 21.05%) |
| `propSd`      | 0.48      | Table 4, proportional residual error epsilon; Methods eq. 3 |
| ODEs for `depot`, `central`, `peripheral1` | n/a | Methods eq. 2 |
| `Cc ~ prop(propSd)` | n/a | Methods eq. 3, `Cobs = Cpred * (1 + eps)` |
| Dose 1147 ug KAU | n/a | Results 3.1 (1.0054 g extract x 1.1408 mg/g) |

# Typical-value simulation

The model has no between-subject variability, so the typical-value
prediction is the model's prediction for every subject. Concentrations are
simulated on a fine grid over the 12 h sampling window. rxode2 warns that
the model has no omega parameters; that is expected for a naive-pooled fit.

```{r typical}
mod <- readModelDb("Choi_2018_kaurenoic_acid")
dose_ug <- 1147 # 1.147 mg KAU in 1.0054 g extract (Results 3.1)
trt <- "1.0054 g extract (1.147 mg KAU)"

ev_typ <- rxode2::et(amt = dose_ug, cmt = "depot") |>
  rxode2::et(seq(0, 12, by = 0.05), cmt = "central")

sim_typ <- rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod), ev_typ) |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::mutate(id = 1L, treatment = trt)
```

# Replicate Figure 4

Figure 4 of Choi 2018 shows the observed concentrations (n = 10) with the
model-predicted curve on a log axis. Below, the typical-value curve is drawn
together with a 90% prediction interval from 200 replicate profiles that
carry only the proportional residual error, sampled at the study's nominal
times.

```{r vpc}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20181128)
obs_times <- c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12)
n_rep <- 200L
ev_rep <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  data.frame(id = seq_len(n_rep), time = 0, amt = dose_ug, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot"),
  tidyr::crossing(id = seq_len(n_rep), time = obs_times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(amt = NA_real_, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

sim_rep <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev_rep) |> as.data.frame()

# The simulated observations scatter around the prediction with the
# published proportional SD: the pooled median of sim/pred must be ~1.
# 2200 draws give a standard error of about 1.3% on that median, so a
# 10% window cannot flicker, yet any mismatch between the error model
# and the observation variable moves it.
ratio <- sim_rep$sim / sim_rep$Cc
stopifnot(abs(median(ratio) - 1) < 0.10)

pi_rep <- sim_rep |>
  dplyr::group_by(time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    Q05 = quantile(sim, 0.05),
    Q50 = quantile(sim, 0.50),
    Q95 = quantile(sim, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot() +
  geom_ribbon(
    data = pi_rep, aes(time, ymin = pmax(Q05, 0.1), ymax = Q95),
    fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.25
  ) +
  # Drop the pre-dose zero, which has no place on a log axis.
  geom_line(data = dplyr::slice(sim_typ, -1), aes(time, Cc), colour = "blue") +
  geom_point(data = pi_rep, aes(time, Q50), colour = "steelblue") +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(0.1, 100)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Plasma KAU (ug/L)",
    title = "Typical prediction and 90% residual-error interval",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 4 of Choi 2018 (predicted curve)."
  )
```

The typical curve reproduces the published line: a peak of about 18 ug/L
near 0.6 h, about 2.2 ug/L at 4 h and about 0.64 ug/L at 12 h. The lower
residual-error bound is truncated at 0.1 ug/L for the log axis; proportional
error with SD 0.48 puts the 5th percentile close to zero near the peak.

# PKNCA validation

Choi 2018 computed its secondary parameters by noncompartmental analysis of
the **model-predicted** profile, with AUC0-inf from the linear trapezoidal
rule up to the last time and extrapolated to infinity (Methods 2.6). The
same analysis is run on the typical-value profile.

```{r pknca}
nca_conc <- sim_typ |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)

dose_df <- data.frame(id = 1L, time = 0, amt = dose_ug, treatment = trt)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = Inf,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(
  conc_obj, dose_obj,
  intervals = intervals,
  options = list(auc.method = "linear")
))

nca_wide <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  dplyr::select(PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)
nca_wide
```

## Comparison against published NCA

```{r nca_compare}
published <- tibble::tribble(
  ~treatment, ~cmax, ~tmax, ~aucinf.obs, ~half.life,
  trt,        18.02, 0.6,   47.89,       4.97
)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = nca_res,
  reference = published,
  by = "treatment",
  units = c(cmax = "ug/L", tmax = "h", aucinf.obs = "ug*h/L", half.life = "h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  caption = "Simulated vs. published (Choi 2018 Table 4, secondary parameters). * differs from reference by >20%."
)

# Deterministic comparison: the typical-value profile has no random
# component, so these bounds are tight. A mis-transcribed CL, V or ka, or a
# dose-unit slip, moves Cmax or AUC by far more than 3%.
stopifnot(
  abs(nca_wide$cmax / 18.02 - 1) < 0.03,
  abs(nca_wide$tmax - 0.6) <= 0.1,
  abs(nca_wide$aucinf.obs / 47.89 - 1) < 0.03,
  abs(nca_wide$half.life / 4.97 - 1) < 0.05
)

# Closed-form identity: AUC0-inf of a linear model equals Dose / (CL/F).
stopifnot(abs(nca_wide$aucinf.obs / (dose_ug / 23.89) - 1) < 0.01)
```

All four secondary parameters agree with Table 4. AUC0-inf also equals
Dose / (CL/F) = 1147 / 23.89 = 48.0 ug*h/L; the printed 47.89 ug*h/L
differs from it only by the trapezoid and extrapolation error of the
paper's NCA.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **No between-subject variability.** The published parameters come from
  the naive-pooled engine (Methods 2.6). The authors also ran an exploratory
  mixed-effects analysis and say they present the basic-model estimates,
  but they report no omega values, so the packaged model carries no etas.
  Simulations with `rxSolve()` therefore vary only through the residual
  error.
- **Residual error as an SD.** Table 4 prints the proportional residual
  error as 0.48 without saying whether it is a variance or a standard
  deviation. Phoenix NLME estimates the residual-error parameter as a
  standard deviation, so it is encoded as `propSd = 0.48`.
- **Covariates.** Age, body weight, height, serum creatinine, creatinine
  clearance, ALT, AST and GGTP were screened. Only creatinine clearance on
  CL/F showed a relationship and it did not significantly improve the basic
  model, so no covariate is in the model; the screened covariates are listed
  in `covariatesDataExcluded`.
- **Dose units.** The model is dosed in micrograms of KAU (1147 ug for the
  1.0054 g extract dose), so `central / vc` is in ug/L (= ng/mL), the units
  of the paper's figures and Table 4.
- **Apparent parameters.** CL, CLD, V and V2 are apparent (/F) values
  (Methods 2.6). Oral bioavailability is not identifiable and no `f(depot)`
  term is included.
- **Height range.** Methods 2.5 gives the height range as 167-183 cm and
  Table 3 as 157.0-183.0 cm. Height is not in the model; the `population`
  metadata records both.
- No erratum or correction notice for this article was found on Europe PMC
  (checked 2026-11-25).
